why: our `Timer` is an entity in the executor's static table with a MODE (`inert`, `oneshot`, `repeating`) that can be changed in place, because a static table cannot grow a timer at runtime and re-arming is how a one-shot is reused. rclcpp's `WallTimer` is created per use and cancelled when done, which needs an allocation each time. Unlike C, the Rust timer's callback IS swappable, because a re-armed one-shot in a static slot is how the mode changes.
